citation.author: Elpidorou, Andreas and Freeman, Lauren
citation.title: Is Profound Boredom Boredom?
citation.in: Hadjioannou, C. (ed.), Heidegger on Affect, Philosophers in Depth (Palgrave Macmillan)

discipline: philosophy (Heidegger scholarship) in dialogue with the psychology of boredom
thesis: Profound boredom shares features with both state boredom and trait boredom but cannot be seamlessly assimilated to either, nor is it sui generis (entirely disconnected from ordinary/psychological boredom); it is best understood as a rare, hybrid existential mode combining trait boredom's totalizing severity with state boredom's motivational, authenticity-disclosing function.
sections: 1 Boredom: A Primer (pp.3-4) -- state vs. trait boredom distinction; BPS/ZBS scales; correlates of boredom proneness
2 Heidegger's Boredom (pp.5-8) -- FCM's three forms: 2.1 becoming-bored-by (first form), 2.2 being-bored-with (second form), 2.3 profound boredom (third form)
3 Understanding Profound Boredom (pp.9-20) -- 3.1 state boredom is not profound enough; 3.2 trait boredom is too negative, too personal; 3.3 profound boredom as sui generis (constructed and rejected)
4 Locating Profound Boredom (pp.20-23) -- conciliatory hybrid reading; Table 1 comparison of profound/trait/state boredom

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: central topic; the impersonal 'es ist einem langweilig,' totalizing and rare, tested against state, trait, and sui generis readings

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: expository (station/flight/doctor examples), then compared to state boredom in sec 3.1

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: dinner-party example; read as a retroactive cognitive attitude rather than a self-luminous affective episode

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: imported psychological scaffold used both as literature-review frame and as the two-pronged test profound boredom must fail before sui generis arises

constructs.label: boredom proneness
constructs.treatment: defined as what BPS operationalizes; linked to Bargdill's 'life boredom' testimonies

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: borrowed (via Elpidorou 2014, 2018a, 2018b) to explain profound boredom's motivational character without trait-likeness

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: recurs across all three levels: state boredom's 'lack of meaning,' the second form's retroactive meaninglessness, profound boredom's world-draining of significance

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: connective construct across state boredom's altered time-perception and Heidegger's Zeitvertreib / collapse of temporal dimensions

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: light touch only, via state boredom's 'attentional difficulties'

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: absent; contrast class throughout is psychological (state/trait) boredom, not flow

measures.label: self-report / survey scale
measures.treatment: BPS (Farmer and Sundberg 1986) and ZBS (Zuckerman 1979) surveyed from the literature as the two adequate trait-boredom measures; discussed, not administered

readings.summary: Paraphrases Heidegger's first-form examples (delayed flight, late doctor, unwanted phone call) and imports the two structural moments (being-left-empty, being-held-in-limbo) largely intact; adds the comparative claim -- absent from FCM itself -- that this form 'appears to be akin to state boredom.'

Stays close to the dinner-party example and the 'standing present' (stehendes Jetzt) analysis (citing FCM 109, 111-112, 114, 124); glosses 'boring' here as casualness / inauthentic following of a social ideal.

Center of gravity of the chapter's FCM exposition: tracks the impersonal 'es ist einem langweilig,' the collapse of past/present/future, being-left-empty/held-in-limbo, the 'telling refusal' (Versagen, FCM 140), and the Augenblick as authentic self-disclosure (FCM 149).

Gestures toward FCM's separate 'contemporary boredom' discussion (FCM sec.18c, secs.37-38) but explicitly declines to reconstruct it, deferring to de Beistegui (2003) instead -- a citation, not an independent reading.

concepts: Befindlichkeit as the ontological structure underlying moods
Augenblick (moment of vision) as authentic self-disclosure
formal indication (formale Anzeige) as the methodological warrant for a possible sui generis reading
the two structural moments: Leergelassenheit (being left empty) and Hingehaltenheit (being held in limbo)
self-luminosity of affect (note 7) -- whether boredom-as-type is typically transparent to the one who has it
life boredom (Bargdill 2000) as a first-personal proxy for trait boredom
interlocutors: Miguel de Beistegui (2003) -- cited approvingly on formal indication's radicalization of fundamental ontology and on contemporary boredom / Kulturphilosophie

Daniel Dahlstrom (1994), Steven Crowell (2001), Theodore Kisiel (1993), Leslie MacAvoy (2010), Ryan Streeter (1997) -- formal-indication scholarship cited as the resources for (not as named advocates of) the sui generis reading E&F construct and reject
Wijnand Van Tilburg and Eric Igou (2011, 2012) -- meaning-regulation account of boredom
John Eastwood, Alexandra Frischen, Mark Fenske, Daniel Smilek (2012) -- 'Unengaged Mind' review
Richard Farmer and Norman Sundberg (1986) -- Boredom Proneness Scale
Matthew Ratcliffe (2013) and Jan Slaby (2014, 2015) -- moods and temporality in Heidegger
Baruch Spinoza -- Ethics Vp42s, closing epigraph
tensions: PRIMARY DEBATE-AXIS POSITION -- 'profound boredom is boredom <-> profound boredom is a distinct existential mood' (this cluster's named axis, grounded here): E&F explicitly construct and then REJECT the sui generis / 'entirely distinct existential mood' pole (pp.15-20), giving four counter-considerations (methodological pointlessness of discussing forms 1-2 first, FCM 156's own ontological-dependency claim, recurrence of profound-boredom features in trait/state boredom, and metaphilosophical self-undermining). They land on the 'profound boredom is boredom' side of the axis, but only in a QUALIFIED, hybrid sense -- profound boredom is continuous with, and conditions the possibility of, ordinary/scientific boredom (p.19, FCM 156) without being identical to either state or trait boredom (secs.3.1-3.2, pp.9-15). This is a conciliatory middle position, not an unqualified identification.

State boredom is not profound enough (not totalizing, not ontologically revealing, no philosophical import) vs. trait boredom is too negative and too personal (pathological, incapacitating, personality-grounded) -- profound boredom is argued to fail identification with EITHER psychological category, for opposite reasons (pp.9-15).

The chapter's own comparative method (testing Heidegger's construct against specific psychological categories) vs. Heidegger's explicit resistance (via formal indication) to having his concepts checked against empirical psychology at all (p.16) -- E&F proceed anyway, arguing the check is legitimate precisely because profound boredom is not sui generis.

Totalizing trait boredom (Bargdill/Maltsberger testimonies) is incapacitating and despair-inducing, while totalizing profound boredom is motivating and authenticity-disclosing -- same structural feature (totalizing scope), opposite existential valence (pp.14-15, 22).
